build.note: Ice time × production per 60 minutes, both recency-weighted and blended with a position average, then scaled by how many shots the opponent allows compared with the league. Then adjusted for how he has done against our own forecasts: 242 shots against 302.3 forecast in his earlier games, shrunk toward no adjustment. The model then turns this average into the chance of each count.

player_context.note: Newer appearances carry more weight. Ice time has a 14-appearance half-life; production per minute has a 110-appearance half-life. The offseason does not age player history. Expected shots scale with the opponent’s shots allowed, and scoring with its goals allowed, relative to the league. A player who has consistently beaten (or missed) our earlier forecasts gets a shrunk adjustment toward that record. Observed averages below are unweighted. Participation and current role remain unconfirmed.

key_drivers: Projected ice time 14.4 minutes; separately shrunk production rate
uncertainties: Line and power-play assignment not verified
invalidation_conditions: New goalie, lineup or injury information
rows.goalie_assumption: Projected, not confirmed. Opposing goalie, Edmonton Oilers: likely Devon Levi 68% (sv 0.900), Tristan Jarry 32%, back-to-back.
rows.lineup_assumption: Participation required for action; current role and active lineup unconfirmed

sensitivity.assumption: Production/opportunity means ±10%; not a confidence interval

assessment.reason: A projected mean near one shot against a 1.5 line supports the under, and the model stays above the -145 break-even across its sensitivity range. The goalie input conflicts with the injury table, but goalie identity matters little for shot volume.
assessment.model_case: The model projects about one shot over 14.4 minutes, below 1.5, and the under holds if production or opportunity moves a tenth either way. The weakness is that line and power-play role are unverified. A last game on Oct 26 also leaves current usage unclear.
assessment.price_case: This is a single main line at -145, which needs roughly 59-in-100 to break even. The model sits well above that. Two other books lean only modestly toward the under, and a market-weighted blend leaves a thin margin, so the gap deserves skepticism.
assessment.context_case: No sourced report covers Kartye's role or status. The injury table lists Levi on IR, which contradicts the model's projected Edmonton goalie. That points to a stale input rather than a shot-volume driver.

qualitative_review.countercase: The market may know Kartye has a top-six or power-play role that the 14.4-minute projection misses, which would push his shot rate toward the line. The stale goalie input raises the question of whether other inputs are outdated. Bovada's non-participation rules are unchecked.
open_checks: Confirm Kartye dresses, plus his line and power-play assignment, from game-day lineups.
Verify Bovada's settlement rules if the player does not play or plays only partially.
Reconfirm that the 1.5 line at -145 is still available before deciding.
Note Edmonton's confirmed starting goalie; this is minor for shot volume.

evidence.excerpt: Edmonton Oilers: Devon Levi (G); Undisclosed; IR. Expected to be out until at least Nov 9
evidence.interpretation: If this listing is current, the model's leading goalie assumption is wrong, suggesting stale inputs. The effect on Kartye's shot volume is likely small, since shot attempts depend little on the opposing goalie.
